newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgargas sets up joint ventures with German firms.
newsitem.headline: Bulgargas sets up joint ventures with German firms.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-owned Bulgargas, Bulgarian firm Gemet and Germany's Zimmermann & Jansen GmbH have set up a joint stock firm in Sofia for the production of gas pipeline armatures, Bulgargas said on Wednesday.
The venture, named Gas Service, will use free capacities in Bulgarian plants and will invest in their modernisation and enlargement, a statement said.
The new stock venture plans to export, as the only such producer in the Balkans, the statement said.
Bulgargas holds 34 percent in the venture, Zimmermann & Jansen has a 51 percent stake and Gemet holds 15 percent.
Bulgargas officials declined to say what the venture's capital was but according to a government decision it should be 100,000 marks.
Bulgargas and Germany's Wintershall AG, which is the energy subsidiary of BASF chemical group, will set up another joint stock company in Sofia by the beginning of April, Bulgargas officials said.
The new stock venture will be for trade, transportation and storage of natural gas and other goods for the energy sector, as well as servicing gas pipelines.
The two firms will have equal shares in the new company, whose capital is expected to be 100,000 marks.
